record.paper_title: Some open problems in computational algebraic geometry
record.original_question: For cyclic algebraic curves that form positive-dimensional loci in the moduli space M_g, define invariants analogous to the dihedral invariants used for hyperelliptic curves with extra involutions, and use them to describe the corresponding cyclic moduli.

evidence.quote: We call such invariants dihedral invariants of hyperelliptic curves.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background. Let $M_g$ denote the coarse moduli space of smooth projective algebraic curves of genus $g \ge 2$ over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero. A smooth curve $X$ of genus $g$ is called cyclic if it admits a cyclic cover $X \to \mathbb{P}^1$, i.e. a non-trivial cyclic subgroup $C_n \le \mathrm{Aut}(X)$ such that $X/C_n \cong \mathbb{P}^1$. For a fixed signature (genus $g$, order $n$, and ramification data), the cyclic curves with that signature form a locally closed sublocus $\mathcal{L} \subset M_g$, which may have positive dimension.

For the special case of hyperelliptic curves of genus $g$ that admit an extra (non-hyperelliptic) involution, one can put the curve in a normal form whose coefficients are acted on by a dihedral group $D_g$, and the invariants of this action — the so-called dihedral invariants $u_1,\dots,u_{2g-1}$ — give a birational parametrization of the corresponding sublocus of $M_g$ and can be used to determine the field of moduli of points in that sublocus.

Problem. For every cyclic family of curves whose corresponding sublocus $\mathcal{L} \subset M_g$ has positive dimension, construct an explicit set of invariants (analogous to the dihedral invariants in the hyperelliptic case with extra involution) that:
(i) are polynomial (or rational) invariants of the natural group action on the coefficients of a chosen normal form for the family;
(ii) provide a birational parametrization of $\mathcal{L}$;
(iii) allow one to read off the field of moduli of any point of $\mathcal{L}$ from the values of the invariants.

Use these invariants to give an explicit description of the cyclic moduli sublocus $\mathcal{L}$ in $M_g$.
artifact.category_tag: Invariants of cyclic curves and moduli
artifact.status_search_result: The general program — defining dihedral-type invariants for cyclic covers of the line giving positive-dimensional loci in M_g — has been advanced in numerous works by Shaska and collaborators. Explicit invariants and birational descriptions have been obtained in specific cases (hyperelliptic curves with extra involutions, genus 2, genus 3 hyperelliptic and bielliptic loci, certain superelliptic/cyclic families, hyperelliptic curves with reduced automorphism group A_5). However, a uniform construction covering all positive-dimensional cyclic loci in M_g for arbitrary genus and signature does not appear to have been completed, so the problem is best classified as partially solved.

status_evidence.title: Hyperelliptic Curves with Extra Involutions (Gutierrez–Shaska)
status_evidence.snippet: Dihedral invariants are introduced for hyperelliptic curves with extra involutions, giving a birational parametrization of the corresponding locus.
status_evidence.claim: Dihedral invariants solve the problem for the hyperelliptic case with extra involution.

status_evidence.title: Bielliptic curves of genus 3 in the hyperelliptic moduli
status_evidence.snippet: Explicit invariants describing a positive-dimensional sublocus of the genus 3 hyperelliptic moduli are constructed.
status_evidence.claim: Partial extensions to other cyclic loci have been carried out.

status_evidence.title: Hyperelliptic curves with reduced automorphism group A5
status_evidence.snippet: Invariants are computed for further families of hyperelliptic curves with prescribed automorphism group.
status_evidence.claim: Case-by-case progress continues for additional cyclic families.

status_evidence.title: On cyclic covers of the projective line
status_evidence.snippet: Studies cyclic covers and their moduli, extending the dihedral-invariant philosophy to broader cyclic settings.
